questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
questions.q: Match the pericardial anatomy table — 1) Outer parietal composition 2) Outer parietal development 3) Inner visceral composition 4) Inner visceral development … A) Fibrous B) Somatopleuric mesoderm C) Collagen + elastic fibres D) Splanchnopleuric mesoderm
questions.exp: The table prints outer parietal fibrous from somatopleuric mesoderm and inner visceral collagen + elastic fibres from splanchnopleuric mesoderm. (Book p358)

questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
questions.q: Match the feature and disease columns — 1) Outer parietal feature 2) Outer parietal disease 3) Inner visceral feature 4) Inner visceral disease … A) Pain sensitive B) Pericarditis C) Pain insensitive D) Acute rheumatic fever (only)

questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence

questions.exp: The line under the table prints pericardial fluid : 50 mL. (Book p358)

questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
questions.q: Which chain prints the first function of the pericardium?
opts: Inspiration → ↓ intrathoracic pressure → transmitted to cardiac chambers → augments filling
Inspiration → ↓ intra-abdominal pressure → augments filling
Inspiration → ↓ intrathoracic pressure → transmitted only to the LV → augments ejection
Expiration → ↓ intrathoracic pressure → augments filling
questions.exp: Function 1 prints inspiration ↓ intrathoracic pressure → transmitted to cardiac chambers → augments filling. (Book p358)

questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
questions.q: Which gradient explains greater right-heart filling in inspiration?
opts: The SVC is extrathoracic while the heart is intrathoracic, creating a gradient between SVC and (R) atrium (RA), so the rt heart fills more during inspiration
The IVC–LA gradient fills the left heart more
No gradient is printed; filling is passive
The pulmonary vein is extrathoracic, creating a gradient with the LA
questions.exp: The diagram labels SVC extrathoracic and heart (RA/LA/RV/LV) with PV intrathoracic, then gradient between SVC and (R) atrium (RA) → therefore rt heart fills more during inspirations. (Book p358)

questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
questions.q: Which chain prints interventricular dependence?
opts: ↑ Rt heart filling → septum pushed to the left → ↓ CO (cardiac output)
↑ Rt heart filling → septum unchanged → ↑ CO
↑ Lt heart filling → septum pushed to the left → ↑ CO
↓ Rt heart filling → septum pushed to the left → ↓ CO
questions.exp: Function 2 prints ↑ rt heart filling → septum pushed to the left → ↓ CO. (Book p358)

questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
questions.q: Which inspiratory SBP fall separates normal from pulsus paradoxus, and where is it seen?
opts: No fall is normal; any fall is pulsus paradoxus
Fall upto 10 mm Hg normal; >10 mm fall only in COPD
Fall upto 20 mm Hg normal; >20 mm fall in tamponade only
Fall in SBP upto 10 mm Hg during inspiration is normal; >10 mm fall is pulsus paradoxus (Normalis aggregans), seen in cardiac tamponade and 1/3 cases of CCP
questions.exp: The block prints fall in SBP upto 10 mm Hg during inspiration, >10mm fall : pulsus paradoxus (Normalis aggregans) with cardiac tamponade and 1/3 cases of CCP. (Book p358)

questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
questions.q: Transmyocardial filling pressure (TFP) = intracavitatory − ____ pressure (IPP); if IPP ↑ then TFP ↓ → diastolic dysfunction.
opts: transpulmonary
intrapericardial
intrapleural
intra-atrial
questions.exp: Function 3 prints TFP = intracavitatory – intrapericardial pressure (IPP) with IPP ↑ → TFP ↓ → diastolic dysfunction. (Book p358)

questions.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
questions.q: Which pressure concordance/discordance pair closes p358?
opts: Discordance of both systolic and diastolic pressures
Concordance of systolic pressures and discordance of diastolic pressures (LV & RV) during inspiration
Concordance of diastolic pressures only during expiration
Concordance of both systolic and diastolic pressures
questions.exp: Function 4 prints concordance of systolic pressures and discordance of diastolic pressures, braced (LV & RV) during inspiration. (Book p358)

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign
questions.q: Which six etiologies are printed for CCP?
opts: Repeated acute viral pericarditis episodes (m/c), HIV, IgG4 disease, aspergillus, malignancy (Ca breast), radiation
Acute viral pericarditis single episode (m/c), TB, IgG4 disease, histoplasmosis, malignancy (Ca breast), surgery
Repeated acute viral pericarditis episodes (m/c), TB (and m/c), IgG4 related disease, histoplasmosis, malignancy (Ca breast), radiation
Repeated acute viral pericarditis episodes (m/c), TB, IgG4 disease, histoplasmosis, malignancy (Ca colon), trauma
questions.exp: The etiology bullets print repeated acute viral pericarditis episodes (m/c), TB (and m/c), IgG4 related disease, histoplasmosis, malignancy (Ca breast) and radiation. (Book p359)

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign

Uremia
Malignancy (Ca breast)
IgG4 related disease

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign
questions.q: Which pathophysiology chain is printed for CCP?
opts: Symmetric fibrosis + thickening + adhesion + calcification → elastic pericardium → impaired ventricular ejection
Symmetric fibrosis + thickening + adhesion + calcification → rock like pericardium → impaired ventricular filling
Symmetric fibrosis + thickening → rock like pericardium → impaired ventricular ejection
Symmetric inflammation + effusion → rock like pericardium → impaired ventricular filling
questions.exp: The chain prints symmetric fibrosis + thickening + adhesion + calcification → rock like pericardium → impaired ventricular filling. (Book p359)

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign
questions.q: Match the CCP hemodynamic phases — 1) Systole and initial 1/3 of diastole 2) Later 2/3 of diastole 3) Late diastole … A) Normal (N) B) Dysfunction C) Elevation & equalization of diastolic preanse in all 4 chambers → no filling (as printed)
questions.exp: The hemodynamics block prints systole (N), diastole initial 1/3 (N), later 2/3 dysfunction, and late diastole elevation & equalization of diastolic preanse in all 4 chambers → no filling (as printed). (Book p359)

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign

opts: ↑ aortic pressure with hypertension, and ↑ IVC pressure with edema
↑ pulmonary vein pressure with dyspnea, and ↑ IVC pressure with edema
↑ SVC pressure with ↑ JVP, and ↓ IVC pressure with dehydration
↑ SVC pressure with ↑ JVP, and ↑ IVC pressure with edema, ascites, hepatomegaly, both ending in rt heart failure (RHF)
questions.exp: The RAP branch prints ↑ SVC pressure/↑ JVP and ↑ IVC pressure/edema, ascites, hepatomegaly converging on rt heart failure (RHF). (Book p359)

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign

Pulsus bigeminus in most patients
Pulsus paradoxus in 1/3rd patients
Pulsus alternans in 1/3rd patients

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign
questions.q: Match the CCP JVP findings — 1) X-descent 2) Y-descent 3) Kussmaul's sign … A) Sharp, rapid, prominent x descent, normal (atrial relaxation in systole) B) Sharp, prominent y descent (atrial emptying in initial diastole) C) JVP ↑ with inspiration
questions.exp: The JVP bullets print the sharp rapid prominent x descent, the sharp prominent y descent and Kussmaul's sign (JVP ↑ with inspiration). (Book p359)

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign

opts: Square root sign with opening snap, early dip → rapid filling → plateau
Dome-and-plateau sign with S3, early dip → slow filling → plateau
Square root sign with pericardial knock, early dip → rapid filling → plateau
Square root sign with pericardial knock, late dip → rapid filling → spike
questions.exp: The block prints ventricular pressures : square root sign with pericardial knock, early dip, rapid filling and plateau beside the square root sign trace. (Book p359)

questions.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign

True — CCP's JVP shows sharp prominent x and y descents with Kussmaul's sign

True — pulsus paradoxus is present in all CCP patients
questions.exp: The page prints pulsus paradoxus in 1/3rd patients, sharp prominent x and y descents, Kussmaul's sign, late-diastolic equalization with no filling and the square-root plateau trace. (Book p359)

questions.sec: CCP ECG and Broadbent's Sign, Differentials, the Tamponade-CCP-RCM Table and Tamponade Opening

questions.sec: CCP ECG and Broadbent's Sign, Differentials, the Tamponade-CCP-RCM Table and Tamponade Opening

questions.sec: Tamponade Pathophysiology, Holodiastolic Equalization, JVP, Beck's Triad, Alternans and Pericardiocentesis

units.title: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
units.sec: Pericardial Anatomy Table, Fluid Volume, Pressure Transmission and Interventricular Dependence
units.guide:
Pericardium: outer parietal fibrous (somatopleuric mesoderm, pain sensitive, pericarditis) vs inner visceral collagen + elastic fibres (splanchnopleuric mesoderm, pain insensitive, acute rheumatic fever only); fluid 50 mL (p358). Function 1: inspiration ↓ intrathoracic pressure → transmitted to chambers → augments filling; SVC extrathoracic vs heart intrathoracic gives the SVC–RA gradient so the rt heart fills more in inspiration.
Function 2: ↑ rt filling → septum to the left → ↓ CO; SBP fall upto 10 mm Hg in inspiration is normal, >10 mm is pulsus paradoxus (Normalis aggregans) in tamponade and 1/3 CCP. Function 3: TFP = intracavitatory − intrapericardial pressure; IPP ↑ → TFP ↓ → diastolic dysfunction. Function 4: systolic concordance with diastolic discordance (LV & RV) in inspiration.

units.title: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign
units.sec: CCP Etiology, Rock-Like Pericardium, Hemodynamics, Pulse, JVP and the Square-Root Sign
units.guide:
CCP etiology: repeated acute viral pericarditis (m/c), TB (and m/c), IgG4 related disease, histoplasmosis, malignancy (Ca breast), radiation (p359). Pathophysiology: symmetric fibrosis + thickening + adhesion + calcification → rock-like pericardium → impaired ventricular filling.
Hemodynamics: systole and initial 1/3 diastole normal, later 2/3 dysfunction → ↑ RAP → ↑ SVC/↑ JVP and ↑ IVC/edema-ascites-hepatomegaly → RHF; late diastole elevation & equalization of diastolic preanse in all 4 chambers → no filling (as printed). Pulse: pulsus paradoxus 1/3rd; JVP sharp prominent x and y descents with Kussmaul's sign; ventricular pressures show the square-root sign with pericardial knock, early dip → rapid filling → plateau.

units.title: CCP ECG and Broadbent's Sign, Differentials, the Tamponade-CCP-RCM Table and Tamponade Opening
units.sec: CCP ECG and Broadbent's Sign, Differentials, the Tamponade-CCP-RCM Table and Tamponade Opening
units.guide:
CCP ECG: low voltage complexes; systolic retraction of apex = Broadbent's sign; D/D chronic liver disease and RCM; Kussmaul's sign also in RCM and TS; definitive Rx pericardial resection (p360). Comparison table: pulsus paradoxus +++/+/+; prominent y descent –/++/–; prominent x descent +++/++/absent; Kussmaul's –/+++/+; third heart sound –/–/+; pericardial knock –/++/–; low ECG voltage ++ in all; electrical alternans ++/–/–; thickened pericardium and calcification only in CCP (+++/++); effusion +++/+++/–; RV size usually small/normal/normal; equalization +++/+++ (post 1/3rd)/–.
Tamponade opens as a core emergency: abrupt rise in pericardial pressure alt fluid accumulation, cause trauma (m/c).

units.title: Tamponade Pathophysiology, Holodiastolic Equalization, JVP, Beck's Triad, Alternans and Pericardiocentesis
units.sec: Tamponade Pathophysiology, Holodiastolic Equalization, JVP, Beck's Triad, Alternans and Pericardiocentesis
units.guide:
Tamponade: rapid fluid → ↑ pericardial pressure → exaggerated interventricular dependence with pulsus paradoxus in all patients, and LV compression with ↓ BP, obstructive shock, dyspnoea, tachycardia (p361). Holodiastolic elevation & equalization of diastolic pressure in all 4 chambers → no filling.
JVP: sharp rapid prominent x descent with absent y descent; Beck's triad = hypotension, prominent JVP, muffled heart sounds; ECG electrical alternans (alternating high & low volume complexes). Treatment: immediate pericardiocentesis, subxiphoid between xiphoid and left costal margin at 30–45°, aim left mid-clavicle toward the RV anterior wall, 16–18 gauge needle.

units.title: Acute Pericarditis Causes, the Paradoxical Friction Rub, ECG Stages, Investigations and Management
units.sec: Acute Pericarditis Causes, the Paradoxical Friction Rub, ECG Stages, Investigations and Management
units.guide:
Acute pericarditis causes: infections (post viral m/c Coxsackie, TB, HIV), drugs (procainamide, hydralazines, anthracyclines, minoxidil), tumors (breast cancer), autoimmune (IgG4, SLE), post traumatic, post MI, uremia (daily intensive heparin free dialysis) (p362). Pain is sharp, pleuritic, relieved by sitting up & leaning forward; the paradoxical rub (more prominent with effusion, as printed) is high-pitched, leathery/scratchy, heard very close, triphasic, best sitting, at the lower left sternal border.
ECG: global ST elevation followed by Spodick's sign (TP depression) with stage I–IV panels; CXR +/- effusion; echo rules out tamponade. Management: aspirin 325 mg TDS/NSAIDs, colchicine, bed rest, steroids C/I.

units.title: CCP Complication, the MI-versus-Pericarditis Table and Dressler's Syndrome
units.sec: CCP Complication, the MI-versus-Pericarditis Table and Dressler's Syndrome
units.guide:
Repeated pericarditis attacks lead to CCP (p363). MI vs pericarditis: sharp stabbing occasionally dull vs pressure-like heavy squeezing; worsened with inspiration vs no; worse supine/improved sitting-forward vs no; hours to days vs minutes (ischemia)/hours (infarction); nitroglycerin no change vs improved; rub present in most vs absent unless pericarditis; widespread concave vs localized convex ST elevation; PR depression frequent vs rare.
Dressler's syndrome: >2–6 wks post MI, autoimmune, fever + pleuritic pain + polyserositis, rub (+), ECG (N)/acute-pericarditis features, Rx NSAIDs.
